D32·53tw — 2026-10-10
chose: 2.7: a verify timeout is never charged — failuresSoFar skips it, nothing is reopened, no session launched. The command runs once more after a load wait (`loadWait`, on in the CLI): the 1-minute load average below the core count, polled every 5 s, bounded by the command's own timeout and then re-run with a warning, with the verify slot not held while waiting. A re-run that times out too stops the run as `stall`, the task left done and unaccepted (unlanded on lanes, the note names its branch). The full gate and its bisect probes stop the same way. A done task whose newest check is a timeout counts as unchecked, so the next serial run, new or resumed, gates it first. The stall note now counts failures, not attempts.
over: (a) Re-running until a verdict with no bound; (b) after N timeouts, charging a timeout as a fail and reopening; (c) leaving the timed-out task unaccepted while the run carries on; (d) a new run stop reason
because: The operator ruled 2.7 from r4-fixes note 01M4K8J8: a timeout under load (81 on 14 cores) bought a whole session. (a) breaks D10: an unattended run must have no state it can sit in forever. (b) is what the operator ruled out: only a fail charges, never a new session. (c) lets dependents and lanes build on unverified, unlanded work. (d) is a schema change across TS, Rust and conformance for what `stall` already says. A second timeout after the load wait is no longer evidence of load, and only the operator can tell a hang from a bound set too tight, so a stop puts it in front of them without spending a session. A stopped run cannot be resumed, and recover only checked its own done tasks, so without the cross-run rule the task would stay done and unverified forever. Lanes are excluded because a new lanes base does not hold the stopped run's task branch.
